editorialUpdates.title: Send a Canva lead magnet with MailerLite: the complete welcome sequence
editorialUpdates.summary: Build the PDF, signup page, confirmed delivery, and three-email sequence. Includes a completed worksheet, every email, genuine vendor screenshots, free-plan limits, and failure checks.
editorialUpdates.audience: Small businesses, shops, creators, and service businesses delivering a useful free resource
editorialUpdates.effort: Allow a few focused hours for the resource and configuration, plus five days to verify the real delays. This is an editorial planning estimate; account approval and DNS changes can take longer.
editorialUpdates.intro: A complete Canva-to-MailerLite path: create a useful PDF, connect a signup page to one group, require confirmation for a new subscriber, deliver the file, and send two helpful follow-ups.
editorialUpdates.expectedOutcome: A two-page planning PDF, a published signup page, and one three-email welcome workflow with explicit confirmation, timing, unsubscribe, and recovery checks.
prerequisites: A free Canva account and original or permitted resource content.
A MailerLite account allowed to send, an approved sender, privacy policy, business details, and access to any required domain-authentication settings.
Space within the current subscriber, send, landing-page, and automation limits.
Two fresh controlled email addresses for enrollment and unsubscribe tests.

contents.label: Choose the route and check limits

releaseChecks: Confirm with a fresh address before email 1.
Open the correct PDF while signed out.
Record the actual two-day and three-day waits.
Unsubscribe after email 1 and verify later messages are suppressed.
Repeat signup with an existing subscriber and verify no restart with repeat entry disabled.
Confirm the final workflow fits ongoing Free limits after any trial ends.
success: One confirmed resource request starts the intended sequence once.
The delivered PDF opens without Canva access.
Messages arrive with the configured gaps.
pitfalls: A group label does not create marketing permission.
A preview message bypasses real signup and enrollment.
A copied active workflow can send duplicate welcome messages.
Free-plan limits can block delivery while a form still appears to work.
editorialUpdates.researchIntent: Lead-magnet delivery, attaching a PDF in MailerLite, welcome automation troubleshooting, free-plan suitability.
editorialUpdates.maintenanceTrigger: Recheck when MailerLite plan limits or editors change, when the PDF or product changes, or when subscriber delivery begins failing.

editorialUpdates.title: Turn Tally inquiries into Gmail drafts with Google Sheets and Zapier
editorialUpdates.summary: Capture each service inquiry, save its record, and prepare a reply for review. Exact field mapping, a filled example, vendor screenshots, duplicate tests, and a free two-step Zap.
editorialUpdates.audience: Small service businesses and owners who can personally review a modest inquiry queue
editorialUpdates.effort: Allow a focused setup session, then run the controlled form, mapping, duplicate, and recovery cases. This is an editorial allowance, not a measured setup time.
editorialUpdates.intro: Connect Tally native capture to a stable Google Sheets intake tab, create a Gmail draft through one Zapier action, and give every active inquiry an owner and a dated next action.
editorialUpdates.expectedOutcome: A published six-field form, matching intake records, correctly mapped Gmail drafts, and a human-maintained follow-up register.
prerequisites: A Tally account and published form.
A Google account with access to Sheets and Gmail; managed accounts may require administrator approval.
A Zapier account with enough task capacity for one action per inquiry.
An approved business-facts sheet, monitored inbox, review owner, privacy policy, and controlled test email.
releaseChecks: A complete controlled form entry produces a matching intake row and draft.
The draft action creates no sent email.
Empty required fields are blocked; optional blank fields do not break the draft.
Two submissions are recognized as distinct IDs and reviewed before replying.
Repeated action tests are checked for duplicate drafts.
A paused or failed handoff is reconciled against the source before replay.
success: Every completed submission is accounted for.
Recipient, subject, and body values are correctly mapped.
The review owner sends an appropriate response and records its time.
Every active inquiry has a status and dated next action.
pitfalls: Sorting or changing the raw intake tab can disrupt a Zap.
A successful draft action is not a sent customer response.
This two-step recipe has no durable cross-system deduplication action.
A task date does not automatically detect a reply or send a follow-up.
editorialUpdates.researchIntent: Tally Google Sheets integration, Google Sheets Gmail drafts, form follow-up without a paid multistep workflow, and duplicate/trigger troubleshooting.
editorialUpdates.maintenanceTrigger: Recheck after form labels, sheet structure, account permissions, Zapier limits, service rules, or queue ownership change.
